name: Garlic-Butter Salmon & Crispy Potatoes
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Put the potatoes on a sheet pan. Toss with 4 tsp olive oil, 1 tsp seasoned salt, and the black pepper. Roast cut-side down for 15 minutes.
Push the potatoes to one side. Add the green beans and toss them with the remaining 2 tsp olive oil and a pinch of seasoned salt.
Pat the salmon dry. Mix melted butter, garlic, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and the remaining seasoned salt. Spoon it over the salmon.
Place salmon on the pan and bake everything 10–12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 125–130°F for moist salmon or 145°F for fully cooked.
Squeeze lemon over the salmon and green beans. Plate it hot.
note: The butter-garlic topping tastes rich; the lemon keeps it from feeling heavy.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Smothered Beef Tips & Rice
steps: Put the beef in a bowl. Add olive oil, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and black pepper. Toss until coated.
In a second bowl, whisk gravy mix, onion soup mix, 1 1/2 cups water, and Worcestershire until smooth.
Add beef to the Instant Pot and pour gravy over it. Do not stir aggressively.
Cook on HIGH pressure for 18 minutes. Let pressure release naturally for 8 minutes, then release the rest.
While it cooks, rinse the rice. Cook 1 cup rice with 1 1/2 cups water according to package directions.
Taste the gravy before adding any salt. Serve beef tips and gravy over rice.
note: Shorter pressure time keeps the meat tender without turning it into baby food.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Honey-Garlic Chicken Bowls
ingredients: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
steps: Mix honey, soy sauce, water, garlic, and cornstarch in a small bowl.
Season chicken with seasoned salt, garlic powder, and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high. Add chicken in one layer. Leave it alone 3 minutes, then turn and cook 4–5 minutes more. Work in two batches so the pan stays hot.
Microwave or steam broccoli until crisp-tender.
Pour sauce into the skillet. Stir 1–2 minutes until glossy and clinging to the chicken.
Divide rice, broccoli, and chicken between two bowls.
note: The sauce is sweet enough to feel fun, not so sweet that dinner tastes like candy.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Creamy Cajun Shrimp Pasta
ingredients: 12 oz large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Boil pasta in salted water until just tender. Reserve 1/4 cup pasta water, then drain.
Pat shrimp dry and season with 1 tsp Cajun seasoning.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high. Cook shrimp 1–2 minutes per side, then remove.
Lower heat to medium. Add butter and garlic for 20 seconds. Pour in half-and-half and remaining Cajun seasoning.
Stir in Parmesan and pasta water. Add spinach and let it wilt.
Return pasta and shrimp to the skillet. Toss 1 minute. Finish with lemon.
note: Restaurant energy, but you are not washing seven pans afterward.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Legs, Corn & Potatoes
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed metal sheet pan with parchment or foil for easier cleanup.
Pat chicken dry. Mix seasoned salt, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, and pepper.
Toss potatoes with 4 tsp oil and one-third of the seasoning. Roast 15 minutes.
Rub chicken with 4 tsp oil and most of the remaining seasoning. Add chicken to the pan and roast 20 minutes.
Brush corn lightly with remaining oil and seasoning. Add it to the pan. Roast 15–18 minutes more, until chicken reaches at least 165°F; 175–185°F gives drumsticks a better texture.
Broil 2 minutes for extra color if needed.
note: The paprika is controlled. Your chicken will look seasoned, not spray-painted red.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Steakhouse Bowls with Garlic Potatoes
steps: Microwave potatoes with 4 tbsp water in a covered bowl for 5 minutes. Drain well.
Season steak with steak seasoning. Heat half the oil in a hot skillet. Sear steak 3–4 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Rest 5 minutes.
Add remaining oil and potatoes to the skillet. Cook 5–6 minutes until browned. Add butter and garlic for the final minute.
Build bowls with romaine, cucumber, onion, potatoes, and sliced steak. Drizzle each with dressing.
note: Cold crunchy salad plus hot garlic potatoes makes this feel like a real meal, not diet cosplay.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Sunday Baked Spaghetti
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Cook spaghetti 2 minutes less than package directions. Drain.
Heat oil in a skillet. Brown beef and onion 6–8 minutes. Drain excess grease if needed.
Add garlic, Italian seasoning, seasoned salt, and 3 cups sauce. Simmer 5 minutes.
Mix pasta with the meat sauce. Spread in an 8-inch baking dish.
Top with mozzarella and Parmesan. Bake 18–20 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
note: Three cups of sauce keeps one pound of beef meaty and coated without becoming tomato soup.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Blackened Chicken Caesar Wraps
steps: Pat chicken dry. Rub with olive oil and blackening seasoning.
Cook in a hot skillet 3–4 minutes per side until 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Toss romaine with Caesar dressing and Parmesan.
Warm tortillas 15 seconds so they roll easily. Fill each with chicken and dressed lettuce.
Serve two wraps per person with apple slices.
note: Use the apple on the side so the whole thing still feels crisp and fresh.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Bowls
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Place salmon on a lined sheet pan and brush with 4 tbsp teriyaki.
Toss broccoli with sesame oil and place beside salmon. Bake 10–12 minutes.
Warm rice and carrots. Divide between bowls.
Add broccoli and salmon. Drizzle with remaining teriyaki and finish with sesame seeds and green onion.
note: Clean, colorful, and fast enough for a night when your patience has left the building.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Cheeseburger Quesadillas
steps: Brown beef in a skillet. Season with seasoned salt and garlic powder. Stir in ketchup and mustard.
Wipe out the pan. Spread beef, cheese, and pickles over half of each tortilla. Fold closed.
Melt a little butter in the skillet over medium. Cook quesadillas 2–3 minutes per side until crisp and melted.
Cut into wedges. Serve with dressed greens.
note: It scratches the burger itch without needing buns, a grill, or a drive-thru confession.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Lemon-Pepper Chicken & Rice Skillet
steps: Season chicken with lemon pepper and garlic powder.
Heat oil in a deep skillet. Brown chicken 2 minutes per side, then remove; it will finish later.
Add rice and broth. Bring to a boil, cover, and lower heat. Simmer 12 minutes.
Stir in peas. Place chicken on top. Cover and cook 5–7 minutes more, until rice is tender and chicken reaches 165°F.
Stir butter into the rice and squeeze lemon over everything.
note: One pan, actual flavor, no sad naked chicken breast.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Shrimp Tacos with Lime Slaw
steps: Mix slaw, yogurt, mayonnaise, juice of half the lime, and a pinch of salt.
Pat shrimp dry. Toss with oil, chili powder, garlic powder, and seasoned salt.
Cook shrimp in a hot skillet 1–2 minutes per side.
Warm tortillas. Fill with slaw, shrimp, avocado, and salsa.
Squeeze remaining lime over the tacos.
note: Creamy, spicy, and crunchy. The bagged slaw is doing honest work here.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Turkey Meatballs with Creamy Orzo
steps: Mix turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning. Form 12 meatballs.
Heat oil in a deep skillet. Brown meatballs on several sides for 6 minutes. Remove.
Add orzo and broth. Bring to a simmer and cook 8 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in half-and-half, Parmesan, spinach, and remaining Italian seasoning.
Return meatballs, cover, and simmer 5–7 minutes until cooked through.
note: Creamy without needing a brick of cream cheese.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Loaded Chicken Baked Potatoes
ingredients: 2 tbsp plain Greek yogurt or sour cream
steps: Pierce potatoes 6 times. Microwave 7–10 minutes, turning halfway, until soft.
Heat oven or air fryer to 425°F. Split potatoes and fluff the centers. Crisp for 5 minutes.
Warm chicken with barbecue sauce.
Fill potatoes with broccoli, barbecue chicken, and cheddar. Return to heat 3–5 minutes to melt.
Finish with yogurt or sour cream and green onion.
note: This is the right use of leftover chicken: make it look intentional.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Garlic Parmesan Chicken Bites
ingredients: 2 lb chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Microwave halved potatoes with 4 tbsp water for 5 minutes. Drain.
Season chicken. Heat oil in a skillet and cook chicken 6–8 minutes until golden and 165°F. Remove.
Add potatoes and asparagus. Cook 5–6 minutes until browned and crisp-tender.
Lower heat. Add butter and garlic for 20 seconds. Return chicken and toss.
Turn off heat and sprinkle Parmesan over everything.
note: Parmesan goes in after the heat drops so it coats the chicken instead of burning onto the pan.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Beef & Broccoli Takeout Night
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb flank steak or sirloin, thinly sliced
steps: Mix soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, cornstarch, and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet until hot. Cook beef in one layer for 2 minutes, toss, then cook 1 minute more. Remove. Work in two batches so the pan stays hot.
Add broccoli with 4 tbsp water. Cover 2 minutes, then uncover.
Return beef. Pour sauce around the edge of the hot pan. Toss 1–2 minutes until glossy.
Serve over rice.
note: Slice the beef thin and do not crowd it. Gray beef is not invited.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Creamy Tuscan Salmon
ingredients: 3 cups cooked rice or mashed potatoes
steps: Season salmon. Heat oil over medium-high and cook salmon 4 minutes on the first side, 2–4 on the second. Remove.
Lower heat. Add garlic for 20 seconds. Add half-and-half and broth.
Stir in Parmesan, spinach, and sun-dried tomatoes. Simmer 2–3 minutes.
Return salmon and spoon sauce over it for 1 minute.
Serve with rice or mashed potatoes.
note: Looks expensive. Is not complicated. That is the correct ratio.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Oven-Fried Chicken Tender Plates
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Put fries on one side of a large sheet pan.
Set up three bowls: flour; beaten egg; panko mixed with seasoned salt, garlic powder, and paprika.
Coat chicken in flour, then egg, then panko. Place on the pan and spray the tops lightly.
Bake chicken and fries 18–22 minutes, flipping both halfway. Chicken must reach 165°F.
Serve with cucumber and dipping sauce.
note: Crispy enough to count as fun, straightforward enough for Jocelyn to help.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Sausage, Peppers & Rice
steps: Heat oil in a deep skillet. Brown sausage 3–4 minutes, then remove.
Cook pepper and onion 4 minutes. Add smoked paprika, garlic powder, and pepper.
Stir in rice and broth. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Return sausage, cover, and cook 3–5 minutes until rice is tender.
Fluff and serve.
note: This is weeknight jambalaya’s less demanding cousin.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Steak Fajita Sheet-Pan Dinner
steps: Heat oven to 450°F. Place the empty sheet pan in the oven for 5 minutes.
Toss steak, peppers, and onion with oil and fajita seasoning.
Spread everything on the hot pan in one layer. Roast 10–12 minutes, stirring once.
Warm tortillas. Fill with steak and vegetables.
Top with salsa, avocado, and lime.
note: Preheating the pan gives you actual browning instead of wet pepper sadness.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Sunday Chicken Alfredo Bake
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Cook pasta 2 minutes less than package directions. Add broccoli during the final 2 minutes. Drain.
Mix pasta, broccoli, chicken, Alfredo sauce, milk, and garlic powder.
Spread in an 8-inch baking dish. Top with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake 20–25 minutes until bubbling. Rest 5 minutes.
note: The milk loosens jarred Alfredo so the bake stays creamy instead of turning into paste.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Maple-Dijon Salmon & Sweet Potatoes
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss sweet potato and Brussels sprouts with olive oil and 1 tsp seasoned salt. Roast 15 minutes.
Mix maple syrup, Dijon, garlic powder, and remaining seasoned salt.
Move vegetables aside. Add salmon and brush with glaze.
Bake 10–12 minutes more, until salmon is done and vegetables are browned.
note: Sweet potato belongs here because it matches the maple-Dijon situation. Regular potato is not always the main character.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Chicken Fried Rice That Actually Browns
steps: Heat a wide skillet until hot. Add neutral oil and cold rice. Press it out and leave it alone 2 minutes.
Push rice to the sides. Scramble eggs in the center.
Add peas and carrots, chicken, garlic powder, and green onion. Toss 2–3 minutes.
Drizzle soy sauce around the hot edge of the pan, then add sesame oil. Toss and serve.
note: Cold rice plus a wide hot pan. That is the whole secret.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: French Onion Beef & Mashed Potatoes
steps: Heat butter and oil in a skillet. Cook onion over medium 8–10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add ground beef and brown fully. Drain excess grease if needed.
Stir in onion soup mix, broth, and Worcestershire. Simmer 5 minutes.
Mix cornstarch and water. Stir it in and simmer 1–2 minutes until gravy coats the beef.
Serve over mashed potatoes with green beans.
note: All the comfort of Salisbury steak without shaping patties like it is arts and crafts night.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Buffalo Chicken Mac Bowls
steps: Cook macaroni and drain.
Melt butter in the pot. Whisk in flour for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in milk. Simmer 2–3 minutes until slightly thick.
Turn heat low. Stir in cheddar until smooth, then add buffalo sauce and chicken.
Fold in pasta. Divide into bowls with broccoli and a light ranch drizzle.
note: Buffalo sauce cuts the richness so it tastes bold, not just heavy.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Garlic Shrimp, Corn & Rice Skillet
steps: Pat shrimp dry and season with seasoned salt and paprika.
Heat olive oil. Cook bell pepper and corn 3 minutes.
Add shrimp in one layer and cook 1–2 minutes per side. Work in two batches so the pan stays hot.
Lower heat. Add butter and garlic for 20 seconds.
Stir in rice until hot. Finish with lemon.
note: The corn gives it sweetness; lemon and garlic keep it grown.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Parmesan-Crusted Pork Chops
ingredients: 4 boneless pork chops, about 6 oz each
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss halved potatoes with half the olive oil and a pinch of seasoned salt. Roast 12 minutes.
Mix panko, Parmesan, garlic powder, and seasoned salt. Beat egg in a second bowl.
Dip pork in egg, then press into crumbs. Add to the pan with broccoli tossed in remaining oil.
Bake 14–18 minutes, until pork reaches 145°F. Rest 3 minutes before serving.
note: 145°F plus a rest keeps pork juicy. We are no longer cooking it until it apologizes.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Chicken Enchilada Skillet
steps: Add enchilada sauce, beans, corn, onion, and chicken to a deep skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Fold in tortilla strips. Simmer 4–5 minutes until softened but not dissolved.
Sprinkle cheese over the top. Cover 2–3 minutes to melt.
Finish with avocado and Greek yogurt.
note: Enchiladas without the rolling assembly line. Blessings.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Brown-Sugar Glazed Meatloaf Minis
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Mix beef, egg, breadcrumbs, milk, onion, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and pepper.
Shape into 4 small loaves on a lined sheet pan.
Mix ketchup, brown sugar, and mustard. Spoon over the loaves.
Bake 22–25 minutes, until centers reach 160°F.
Serve two minis per person with mashed potatoes and peas.
note: Mini loaves cook faster and every piece gets glaze. Superior engineering.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Finale: Creamy Garlic Steak Pasta
steps: Cook pasta until just tender. Reserve pasta water, then drain.
Season steak. Heat olive oil in a hot skillet and cook steak 3–4 minutes per side. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Lower heat. Add butter and garlic for 20 seconds. Add half-and-half and Parmesan.
Stir in pasta water and spinach. Add pasta and toss until glossy.
Top with sliced steak and any resting juices.
note: Day 30 should not taste like somebody gave up on life.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.

name: Crockpot Mississippi-Style Pot Roast
leftovers: Dinner tonight + 2 leftover nights, or freeze 2 servings.
steps: Optional but worth it: heat olive oil in a skillet and brown the roast 3 minutes per side.
Put potatoes and carrots in the crockpot. Place roast on top.
Sprinkle ranch and au jus seasoning over the roast. Add pepperoncini, juice, and butter.
Cook on LOW 8–9 hours or HIGH 5–6 hours, until the roast pulls apart easily.
Shred the beef into the juices. Serve with vegetables. Cool leftovers before refrigerating.
note: This is a true batch meal. Night two becomes roast bowls or sandwiches instead of feeling like the exact same dinner.

name: Crockpot Salsa Verde Chicken
leftovers: Tacos first, rice bowls next, quesadillas last.
ingredients: 1 can black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Add chicken, salsa verde, garlic powder, cumin, and seasoned salt to the crockpot.
Cook on LOW 5–6 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours.
Shred the chicken directly in the pot.
Stir in black beans and corn. Cover 15 minutes to heat through.
Squeeze lime over everything. Use for tacos, bowls, nachos, or quesadillas.
note: One base, several personalities. That is how leftovers avoid becoming punishment.

name: Crockpot Creamy Garlic Chicken
leftovers: Serve over rice, then pasta, then freeze the remaining sauce and chicken.
ingredients: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs
steps: Season chicken with seasoned salt, garlic powder, and onion powder. Put it in the crockpot.
Whisk broth and cream of chicken soup together and pour over chicken.
Cook on LOW 5–6 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours.
Shred or slice chicken. Stir in cream cheese and Parmesan until smooth.
Add spinach, cover 10 minutes, and stir. Serve over rice, pasta, or mashed potatoes.
note: Rich enough to feel comforting, flexible enough to stretch across different sides.

name: Crockpot Beef & Vegetable Chili
leftovers: Two dinners plus 4 freezer portions.
steps: Brown ground beef with onion in a skillet. Drain excess grease.
Add beef, onion, bell pepper, beans, tomatoes, seasonings, and broth to the crockpot.
Cook on LOW 6–7 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours.
Taste and adjust salt only after everything has cooked.
Serve with rice, cornbread, cheese, or avocado. Freeze cooled portions flat in freezer bags.
note: A practical freezer builder, not a recipe that leaves you trapped eating chili until Thursday.

name: Crockpot Honey-Garlic Chicken
leftovers: Serve with rice first, then use the extra chicken in wraps or bowls.
ingredients: 1 tbsp rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar
steps: Place chicken in the crockpot.
Whisk honey, soy sauce, ketchup, vinegar, garlic, and sesame oil. Pour over the chicken.
Cook on LOW 5–6 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours.
Remove chicken and cut or shred it.
Mix cornstarch and water. Stir it into the sauce, cover, and cook on HIGH 10–15 minutes until slightly thickened. Return chicken to the sauce and finish with green onions.
note: A glossy, flavorful chicken that works just as well over rice as it does tucked into a wrap.

name: Crockpot Chicken Tortilla Soup
leftovers: Refrigerate four servings and freeze the rest in individual portions.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs
steps: Add chicken, beans, corn, tomatoes, enchilada sauce, broth, and seasonings to the crockpot.
Cook on LOW 6 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours.
Remove chicken, shred it, and return it to the soup.
Squeeze in the lime juice and stir.
Serve with tortilla strips, avocado, cheese, or Greek yogurt.
note: Warm, satisfying, and easy to portion for future lunches.

name: Crockpot Italian Beef Sandwiches
leftovers: Serve as sandwiches first, then turn the beef into rice bowls or baked potatoes.
steps: Place the roast in the crockpot.
Sprinkle Italian seasoning and au jus mix over the roast. Add broth, pepperoncini, and pepperoncini juice.
Cook on LOW 8–9 hours or HIGH 5–6 hours.
Shred the beef into the cooking juices.
Pile beef onto rolls, top with provolone, and toast briefly if desired.
note: A rich, tender batch meal that feels different each time you serve it.

name: Crockpot Turkey Meatball Marinara
leftovers: Serve over pasta, then use the remaining meatballs in subs or with roasted vegetables.
ingredients: 8 oz pasta for the first meal
steps: Mix turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, Parmesan, Italian seasoning, seasoned salt, and garlic powder.
Form 18 small meatballs.
Pour one-third of the marinara into the crockpot. Add meatballs in layers, spooning the remaining sauce between them.
Cook on LOW 5–6 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours, until meatballs reach 165°F.
Serve over pasta or in toasted rolls.
note: Tender meatballs, a reliable sauce, and several easy ways to use the leftovers.

name: Crockpot Lemon-Herb Chicken & Potatoes
leftovers: Serve as plated chicken first, then chop the extra chicken for salads or wraps.
steps: Place potatoes and carrots in the crockpot.
Season chicken with olive oil, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, seasoned salt, and pepper. Place it over the vegetables.
Pour broth around the sides and place lemon slices on top.
Cook on LOW 6 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours.
Remove lemon slices before serving. Spoon a little cooking broth over each plate.
note: Soft, bright flavors that keep a batch meal from feeling heavy.

name: Crockpot Barbecue Pulled Chicken
leftovers: Use it for sandwiches, loaded potatoes, flatbreads, or quesadillas. Freeze any extra.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs
steps: Place chicken in the crockpot.
Mix barbecue sauce, broth, Worcestershire, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder. Pour over the chicken.
Cook on LOW 5–6 hours or HIGH 3–4 hours.
Shred chicken and stir it back into the sauce.
Let it sit uncovered on HIGH for 10 minutes if you want the sauce slightly thicker.
note: A dependable batch recipe with enough flexibility to carry several different meals.

name: Garlic-Herb Shrimp with Lemon Rice
leftovers: Serve two portions tonight and refrigerate two portions for lunch or dinner.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and season with seasoned salt, black pepper, and Italian seasoning.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add shrimp in one layer and cook 1–2 minutes per side. Remove from the skillet.
Lower heat to medium. Add butter and garlic and cook for 20 seconds.
Return shrimp to the skillet, squeeze in the lemon juice, and toss for 30 seconds.
Serve over warm rice and finish with parsley if using.
note: Buttery garlic flavor with enough lemon to keep it fresh and clean.

name: Classic Oven Pot Roast
leftovers: Serve with potatoes the first night, then use extra beef for bowls or sandwiches.
steps: Heat oven to 325°F.
Season the roast with seasoned salt, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven and brown the roast 3–4 minutes per side.
Remove the roast. Add onion, potatoes, and carrots to the pot.
Place roast on top. Whisk broth, Worcestershire, and onion soup mix together and pour it around the roast.
Cover and bake 3–3 1/2 hours, until the beef pulls apart easily.
note: Deep, savory pot-roast flavor with tender vegetables and rich pan gravy.

name: Instant Pot Southern Chicken & Rice
leftovers: Refrigerate extra portions with a spoonful of broth so the rice stays moist.
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs or drumsticks
steps: Season chicken with seasoned salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper.
Set Instant Pot to Sauté. Add olive oil and brown chicken 3 minutes per side. Remove.
Add rinsed rice and broth. Stir once and scrape the bottom clean.
Place chicken on top of the rice. Do not stir.
Cook on HIGH pressure for 8 minutes. Let pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then release the rest.
Remove chicken, stir butter into the rice, and serve together.
note: Tender seasoned chicken and buttery rice with no vegetables mixed in.

name: Brown Stew Chicken
leftovers: The flavor deepens overnight, making this especially good for a second dinner.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
steps: Season chicken with seasoned salt, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, paprika, browning sauce, and soy sauce. Let it sit 20 minutes if time allows.
Heat olive oil in a deep skillet or Dutch oven. Brown chicken well on both sides, then remove.
Cook onion and bell pepper for 4 minutes. Add garlic for 20 seconds.
Stir in broth, ketchup, and brown sugar. Return chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low 35–40 minutes, turning once, until chicken is tender and reaches at least 165°F.
Uncover for the final 5 minutes if the gravy needs to reduce.
note: Deeply seasoned chicken with a savory, slightly sweet brown gravy.

name: Classic Beef Stew
leftovers: Refrigerate up to three days or freeze two portions for later.
steps: Season beef with seasoned salt, garlic powder, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven. Brown beef in batches and remove.
Cook onion for 3 minutes. Stir in tomato paste for 30 seconds.
Return beef. Add broth and Worcestershire. Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour.
Add potatoes and carrots. Simmer 35–45 minutes more, until tender.
Whisk gravy mix with 1 cup water. Stir it in and simmer 5 minutes.
note: A thick, savory stew with tender beef and classic gravy.

name: Chili Cheese Dogs
leftovers: Store chili separately and reheat it for another round of dogs, fries, or baked potatoes.
ingredients: 1/4 cup diced onion for topping, optional
steps: Brown ground beef and diced onion in a skillet. Drain excess grease.
Stir in tomato sauce, ketchup, chili powder, garlic powder, and seasoned salt.
Simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
Heat hot dogs according to package directions and warm the buns.
Place hot dogs in buns. Top with chili, cheddar, and extra diced onion if desired.
note: Classic, flavorful chili dogs with enough meat in the chili to make them feel like dinner.

name: Vanilla-Cinnamon French Toast
leftovers: Freeze cooled slices between parchment and reheat in the toaster or oven.
ingredients: 8 thick slices brioche or Texas toast
Maple syrup and berries for serving
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt in a shallow bowl.
Heat a skillet or griddle over medium and melt a little butter.
Dip each bread slice briefly on both sides. Do not soak it until it falls apart.
Cook 2–3 minutes per side until deeply golden.
Repeat with remaining bread, adding butter as needed. Serve warm with syrup and berries.
note: Soft inside, crisp at the edges, and properly flavored all the way through.

name: Buttermilk Chicken & Waffles
leftovers: Reheat chicken in the oven and waffles in the toaster so both stay crisp.
steps: Place chicken in buttermilk and hot sauce for at least 30 minutes or up to overnight.
Mix flour, seasoned salt, garlic powder, paprika, and black pepper.
Remove chicken from buttermilk, letting excess drip off. Coat well in flour.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 350°F. Fry chicken in batches 4–6 minutes, turning once, until golden and 165°F.
Drain on a rack, not paper towels.
Serve over warm waffles with maple syrup or hot honey.
note: Crispy seasoned chicken, fluffy waffles, and the right balance of sweet and savory.

name: Southern Fried Chicken
leftovers: Cool completely before refrigerating. Reheat uncovered at 375°F until crisp.
steps: Soak chicken in buttermilk and hot sauce for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Mix flour and all seasonings in a large bowl.
Remove chicken from buttermilk and coat thoroughly in seasoned flour. Let it rest 10 minutes.
Heat oil to 325–335°F in a deep heavy pot.
Fry chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until golden and the thickest pieces reach 165°F. Breasts usually take 12–15 minutes; thighs and drumsticks 14–18 minutes.
Drain on a wire rack and rest 10 minutes before serving.
note: Deeply seasoned, crisp outside, juicy inside, and worth doing properly.

name: Creamed Spinach
leftovers: Reheat gently with a splash of milk to loosen the sauce.
steps: Wilt spinach in a large skillet in batches. Transfer it to a cutting board and chop lightly.
Melt butter in the skillet. Add garlic for 20 seconds.
Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in half-and-half and simmer 2–3 minutes until thickened.
Stir in Parmesan, seasoned salt, pepper, and nutmeg if using.
Fold spinach into the sauce and cook 2 minutes.
note: Creamy and savory without hiding the spinach under a heavy blanket of sauce.

name: Garlic Sautéed Spinach
leftovers: Best fresh, but extra spinach can be folded into eggs, pasta, or rice.
steps: Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and cook for 20 seconds.
Add spinach in batches, tossing as it wilts.
Season with seasoned salt and black pepper.
Remove from heat and squeeze lemon over the spinach.
note: Simple, glossy, garlicky spinach that works beside almost anything.

name: Instant Pot Beef Stroganoff
leftovers: Refrigerate with a splash of broth or milk mixed in before reheating.
steps: Season beef with seasoned salt, garlic powder, and pepper.
Set Instant Pot to Sauté. Brown beef in olive oil in batches, then remove.
Cook onion and mushrooms for 3 minutes. Add broth and Worcestershire, scraping the bottom clean.
Return beef. Cook on HIGH pressure for 20 minutes, then naturally release for 10 minutes.
Open the pot and stir in egg noodles. Use Sauté and cook 5–7 minutes until tender.
Mix cornstarch and water and stir it in. Turn off heat, then fold in sour cream.
note: Tender beef and creamy noodles with a distinctly different texture from crockpot meals.

name: Garlic-Butter Steak Bites & Potatoes
leftovers: Reheat gently in a skillet so the steak stays tender and the potatoes regain their edges.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb sirloin steak, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Microwave the potatoes with 2 tablespoons water in a covered bowl for 6 minutes. Drain well.
Pat the steak dry and season with steak seasoning, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high. Brown potatoes for 6–8 minutes, then remove.
Add steak in one layer and cook 2 minutes without moving it. Turn and cook 1–2 minutes more.
Lower heat. Add butter and garlic for 20 seconds. Return potatoes and toss everything together.
note: Crispy potatoes and tender garlic-butter steak without turning dinner into a steakhouse production.

name: Ribeye with Herb Butter & Roasted Broccoli
leftovers: Slice leftover steak cold for salads or reheat briefly in a hot skillet.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss broccoli with half the olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Roast 18–20 minutes.
Mix softened butter, garlic, and Italian seasoning.
Pat steaks dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining oil in a heavy skillet over high heat. Sear steaks 3–4 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness.
Rest steaks 7 minutes. Top with herb butter and serve with roasted broccoli.
note: A clean, classic steak dinner with enough richness to feel special and no unnecessary fuss.

name: Pepper Steak with Onion Gravy
leftovers: Serve the extra steak and gravy over rice or mashed potatoes the next day.
steps: Season steak with seasoned salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat. Brown steak quickly in batches and remove.
Lower heat to medium. Cook onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes.
Add broth and Worcestershire. Bring to a simmer.
Mix cornstarch and water. Stir it into the skillet until the gravy thickens.
Return steak and any juices for 1 minute. Serve over rice.
note: Tender steak, soft onions, and a real gravy that earns the rice underneath it.

name: Steak Tacos with Lime Crema
leftovers: Use leftover steak in quesadillas, rice bowls, or a chopped salad.
ingredients: 1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt or sour cream
steps: Pat steak dry. Rub with olive oil and fajita seasoning.
Cook in a hot skillet 4–5 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Rest 7 minutes.
Mix Greek yogurt with juice from half the lime and a pinch of salt.
Warm tortillas and slice steak thinly against the grain.
Fill tortillas with steak, avocado, salsa, onion, and lime crema. Finish with remaining lime.
note: A flavorful steak night that feels fresh, easy, and completely different from steak-and-potatoes.

name: Lemon-Garlic Baked Cod
leftovers: Flake leftover cod into rice bowls or fish tacos; reheat gently to avoid drying it out.
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Place cod in a lightly greased baking dish.
Mix melted butter, olive oil, garlic, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Spoon the mixture over the cod and add thin lemon slices on top.
Bake 12–15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 145°F.
Finish with fresh lemon juice and parsley if using.
note: Mild, easy-to-find fish with garlic-butter flavor and no heavy coating.

name: Blackened Mahi-Mahi Rice Bowls
leftovers: Serve leftover fish cold or gently warmed over rice with avocado and salsa.
steps: Pat mahi-mahi dry and season both sides with blackening seasoning.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high. Cook fish 3–4 minutes per side, until opaque and 145°F.
Warm rice and corn.
Divide rice, corn, cabbage, avocado, and salsa among four bowls.
Add fish and squeeze lime over each bowl.
note: Firm fish, bold seasoning, and fresh toppings that make the bowl feel complete.

name: Oven-Fried Catfish with Cornmeal Crust
leftovers: Reheat uncovered at 400°F so the coating crisps again.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Place a wire rack over a sheet pan and coat it with cooking spray.
Pour buttermilk into a shallow dish.
Mix cornmeal, flour, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and paprika in a second dish.
Dip catfish in buttermilk, then press into the cornmeal mixture.
Place on the rack and spray the tops lightly. Bake 15–18 minutes, until crisp and 145°F.
Serve with lemon.
note: Southern catfish flavor with a crisp cornmeal coating and much less oil than frying.

name: Maple-Dijon Roasted Trout
leftovers: Flake leftover trout over greens or rice and serve chilled or lightly warmed.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Place trout skin-side down on a lined sheet pan.
Mix maple syrup, Dijon, olive oil, garlic, seasoned salt, and pepper.
Brush the glaze evenly over the trout.
Roast 10–13 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 145°F.
Finish with lemon juice.
note: A gentle sweet-and-tangy glaze that works especially well with accessible, flavorful trout.
